articles.title: Paramount+ Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Paramount+ is a streaming subscription service owned by Paramount Skydance. It first launched in the U.S. on March 4, 2021 as a rebrand of CBS All Access.
articles.body:
Paramount+ is a streaming subscription service owned by Paramount Skydance . It first launched in the U.S. on March 4, 2021 as a rebrand of CBS All Access. According to the most recent earnings call , Paramount+ currently has 79.1 million subscribers to its service.

Paramount Skydance recently completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery , but this change has not yet come to the streaming service.

Paramount+ currently offers two different subscription tiers with monthly and annual pricing. There is also a bundle available with Walmart+ or a Prime Video subscription. Paramount+ increased its subscription prices on January 15, 2026 , which is reflected below.

Currently the only way to bundle Paramount+ with other services for additional savings is to pick up a Walmart+ membership, which includes access to an Essential plan. You can also choose the Paramount+ Prime Video add-on to bundle it with your existing Amazon Prime subscription, but there isn't any sort of discount. Both of these options are currently the only way to access a Paramount+ free trial in 2026 . If you decide you don't want Paramount+, luckily, it's easy to cancel .

Paramount+ adds new content to it's streaming service throughout the year. Since it's owned by Paramount Pictures, it gets first streaming rights to popular movie franchises like Mission Impossible and Sonic the Hedgehog. The service also includes CBS, BET, Comedy Central, MTV, and Nickelodeon content. You can also access the full Showtime library if you have a premium subscription.

Some of the most notable offerings on Paramount+ are its original content . This includes the entirety of the Star Trek franchise , and the most recent season of Star Trek: Star Fleet Academy is continuing to grow that list. Other really popular shows included are the Yellowstone prequels, Tulsa King, Mayor of Kingstown, and Halo. Some of these series even stream in 4K with a Premium subscription. Paramount+ has also recently added the Avatar Aang movie as well as the first season of Avatar: Seven Havens , expanding on the original Nickelodean Universe.

In addition to original content, Paramount+ is now the home of UFC fights . These fights were previously only available as PPV on ESPN+ (now ESPN Unlimited ), so this is a significant change in 2026.

articles.body:
Netflix launched as a streaming service in 2007 following the company’s transition from being a DVD rental service. Originally called “Watch Now” in the U.S., the service has since expanded to over 160 countries. Netflix last reported crossing over 325 million paid subscribers at the end of 2025, making it the overall most-subscribed-to streaming service in 2026.

Unlike most other streaming services, Netflix was originally founded as a mail-order DVD rental company in 1997 (launching the following year). After several attempts to re-structure their pricing model for DVD rentals and streaming services, Netflix became a streaming-only service and spun their DVD rental department into it's own company, DVD.com. It pivoted to streaming content on demand in 2007, and became one of the primary players in the streaming wars of the 2010s. Netflix began producing its own original series and movies in 2011, which now make up the bulk of watched hours on the service.

Standalone Netflix subscriptions start at $8.99 and have undergone a number of price hikes (the most recent one in March 2026 ). Unlike most other streaming services, Netflix is not available in any streaming bundles , but it is included as a perk in some internet and phone plans. The service also does not historically offer any discounts.

Netflix has an incredibly wide spread of series and movies stemming from licensing agreements with the likes of Universal and DreamWorks, Paramount, Warner Bros., and Sony. It’s currently the streaming home for franchises like Kung Fu Panda, 28 Years Later, and How to Train Your Dragon.

The service began producing its own original content in 2013, with early hits like House of Cards and Orange Is the New Black paving the way for straight-to-streaming releases. Netflix has since expanded its production hubs across the world, with original content reportedly making up over half of the streamer’s library since 2023.

As of March 2026, Netflix also originals make up the bulk of viewing hours. Some of the most-watched films and series on the service include KPop Demon Hunters, Squid Game, Wednesday, and Stranger Things. More popular Netflix originals right now include the live action version of One Piece , Bridgerton, and Pokemon Horizons.

Netflix is available in a browser format in addition to an app format available through most smart TVs, game consoles, and mobile devices. Here’s the full list of compatible devices .

Netflix offers 4K UHD viewing of select content exclusively through its most expensive Premium Plan. This plan costs $26.99/month in the U.S. and also removes ads. Subscribers should keep in mind that they will only be able to take advantage of 4K UHD quality if they have an existing 4K set-up.

Some popular Netflix shows have gotten 4K Blu-ray releases, which offers a better picture quality than streaming.

articles.body:
Pikmin 4 has a variety of Sublevel Caves for you to explore and these include Dandori-style caves. There are two types of Dandori caves, Dandori Challenges and Dandori Battles . On this page of IGN's Pikmin 4 guide , we'll explain what Dandori Challenges are, and where to find them.

There are 12 Dandori Challenge caves for you to complete across the game. In Dandori Challenges , you'll have a certain amount of time to collect every treasure and creature in the cave. These will get increasingly harder as you progress through the game, with more to collect in a shorter amount of time. This is where your Dandori is really put into practice, and you'll need to gather Pikmin and delegate them efficiently to get a Platinum Score in every challenge.

In the table below, we've listed each of the Dandori Challenges in the game. Click on the location of the Dandori Challenge to jump to a map pinpointing where you can find the Dandori Challenge cave. If you click on the name of the Dandori Challenge , you'll be taken to a dedicated page that shows you how to get a Platinum Score for it.

articles.title: Phantom Liberty Endings Explained - How to Get All Endings - Cyberpunk 2077 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Cyberpunk 2077 Phantom Liberty expansion contains many different endings you can unlock depending on your dialogue choices during key moments in the story.
articles.body:
The Cyberpunk 2077 Phantom Liberty expansion contains many different endings you can unlock depending on your dialogue choices during key moments in the story. On this page, you'll find every ending Phantom Liberty offers to conclude V's story, including how to get them, the explanation for each ending, the consequences on V and their romance options , and the rewards you'll receive.

Phantom Liberty Endings Explained - How to Get All Endings

There are four endings to Phantom Liberty, and all four outcomes rely heavily on your dialogue choices during three vital Main Jobs :

Firestarter: In this quest, where you and Alex infiltrate Hansen's meeting with the netrunner twins, you'll have the option to either escape with Songbird or help Reed capture her.

Helping Songbird escape will unlock the Killing Moon main job, where you can get the King of Swords or the King of Wands endings.

Helping Reed capture her will unlock the Black Steel in the Hour of Chaos main job, leading to Somewhat Damaged , where you can get the King of Pentacles or the King of Cups ending.

Killing Moon: If you helped Songbird escape during Firestarter, there will be a crucial dialogue moment at the end of the quest where you can either kill Reed—allowing Songbird to fly to Luna—or hand her over to the NUSA. This choice is what dictates whether you get the King of Swords or the King of Wands ending, with different subsequent missions.

Somewhat Damaged: If you gave So Mi to Reed during Firestarter, there will be a crucial choice to make during Somewhat Damaged that dictates whether you get the King of Pentacles or the Cups of Cups ending, with different subsequent quests.

In Firestarter , side with So Mi - 'Help Songbird escape'

In The Killing Moon , pick up So Mi and carry her to the shuttle

In The Killing Moon , pick up So Mi and carry her to the shuttle or call Reed right away

In Firestarter , side with Reed - 'Help Reed capture Songbird'

In Somewhat Damaged , agree to So Mi's request to die

In Somewhat Damaged , refuse So Mi's request to die

Use the links below to jump to a more in-depth section for each ending and its explanation:

King of Wands - Kill Reed in the Killing Moon

Arguably the best ending in Phantom Liberty and the one that fits the philosophies of V and Johnny the most, the King of Wands allows V to see his situation from another person's perspective.

Though she hasn't been entirely honest, So Mi, a puppet who was taken advantage of by Myers and the NUSA, gets a second chance. You'll also free Reed from the clutches of his own principles while Alex gets her sunny retirement in Monte Carlo.

When you arrive at the Tycho terminal station with Songbird, she'll reveal that the neural matrix can only be used once and that she was lying about curing both of you the whole time.

Picking her up and then killing Reed during the confrontation will result in the King of Wands ending.

If you draw your weapon while talking to him, you'll need to kill him during the slow-mo sequence; otherwise, he'll kill you, and then you'll have to reload from your last save point.

Don't Miss: Be sure to pick up his iconic tech pistol, Pariah , next to his body after putting So Mi inside the spaceship.

Consequences for the King of Wands Ending

After watching the launch with Johnny, the credits will roll, and you'll spawn by the marina overlooking the spaceport.

Songbird will live and stay on the Moon, leaving you and Johnny back at square one with no cure. Proof of her successful operation will show up later during the Main Job, From Her to Eternity —where you'll find a hermetic container with a metal pin from the lunar city of Tycho inside.

She'll also leave you her personal cyberdeck, the iconic Quantum Tuner .

You'll also talk to Alex and share a drink with her for the last time at The Moth during the mission, Unfinished Sympathy . After completing that mission, you can go back to your apartment to find a postcard from Alex, telling you that she's turned her back on the FIA and made it to Monte Carlo in Monaco.

King of Swords - Hand Songbird Over to Reed in the Killing Moon

If you decide to hand Songbird over to Reed at any point after her confession about the cure, you'll unlock the King of Swords ending at the conclusion of Killing Moon .

Reed will ask you why you turned your back on her, and you can tell him the truth about the cure. He'll then take her inside an FIA AV and tell you you'll hear from him shortly about the operation.

Complete the main jobs Through Pain to Heaven and Who Wants to Live Forever to unlock Things Done Changed (Tower Ending).

King of Cups - End Songbird's Misery in Somewhat Damaged

When you find Songbird inside the Cynosure core at the end of Somewhat Damaged , she'll tell you that the damage she's taken from the Blackwall exposure has essentially erased the majority of her own mind.

Not wanting to be a slave to either the rogue AIs or the FIA, she will ask V to end her life as a way for her to go out as herself.

If you decide to honor her last wish, you'll plug out the cable connecting her to the core, and that'll be the end for Songbird.

Consequences for the King of Cups Ending

Similar to choosing Songbird over Reed at the end of Killing Moon, honoring her wish to die in Somewhat Damaged will also lock V out of getting the cure for the Relic.

Both you and Reed will drive her body back to Myers during Leave in Silence . She will dismiss your efforts in retrieving So Mi as a failure and reward you with a measly 5,000 eddies. King of Cups Ending

King of Pentacles - Refuse to Kill Songbird in Somewhat Damaged

Refusing to honor Songbird's wish to die will nudge you toward the King of Pentacles ending path. When Songbird tells you she's too weak to end her own life, you'll be given the following dialogue options.

Once she gives you her reasoning, pick any of the two options that'll spare her, and Reed will come to help you both.

Consequences for the King of Pentacles ending

Objectively the worst ending in Phantom Liberty, the King of Pentacles perpetuates the cycle of the dog-eat-dog world of Cyberpunk.

So Mi will eventually be cured by the FIA, but her life purpose went from being the government's netrunning lap dog to a literal Blackwall slave.

Reed never learns of his mistakes and blindly follows his principles. Alex is dead at the hands of Hansen—never getting her wish of leaving Night City alive.

However, V will get recognition with a medal from Myers and a guaranteed cure for the Relic.

Through the two main jobs you unlock from this ending path, Who Wants to Live Forever and Things Done Changed , you'll later learn that though V is finally cured of the Relic degradation, the operation costs him to lose all of his friends due to a two-year coma.

Not only that, V has also lost the ability to use any sort of Cyberware, ultimately ending his mercenary career.

Below are the rewards you'll receive, depending on which choices you make during the two vital Main Jobs : Firestarter and Killing Moon .

articles.title: The 15 Best Zombie Movies of All Time
articles.summary: Have you seen all of our top 15 movie picks in the undead genre? These are the best zombie movies ever.
articles.body:
Whether it's corpses rising from their graves due to unexplained otherworldly circumstances or humans transformed into rabid monsters because of a crazed contagion, zombie movies have been a massive part of the horror landscape for decades.

Mary Shelley's Frankenstein, from 200 years ago , was an early exploration of reanimation and its dastardly consequences, but as far as movies go it was George Romero's 1968 flick Night of the Living Dead that popularized what we now know as a "zombie," kicking off an entire wave of undead horror movies that played into some of our most intimate, existential fears.

So stay alert, don't get cornered, aim for the head, and always save one bullet for yourself because we've picked out 15 of the best (and sometimes funniest) zombie movies ever made! Be sure to check out our list of the best zombie games , too.

It's right there in the intro and it's largely considered a masterwork of horror so we may as well start with the granddaddy of the modern zombie genre, George Romero's Night of the Living Dead . This flick reworked and reimagined what a zombie movie could be, removing the shambling creatures from the realm of voodoo and black magic and Haitian jungles and placing them squarely in the backyard of middle-class America, with no clear explanation of the ghouls' origins but plenty of sociological and political subtext surrounding the undead things.

A low budget indie that was, according to Romero, heavily influenced by Richard Matheson's vampire novel I Am Legend and the subsequent Vincent Price film version of Legend called The Last Man on Earth, Night of the Living Dead proved to be immensely influential itself on everything from modern, high-profile "zombie" pictures like 28 Days Later to countless low-budget cheapie rip-offs to, decades after its initial release, video game franchises such as Resident Evil. Of course, AMC's The Walking Dead is also the perfect example of the impact of Romero zombies. Remember, for a few years it was the most popular show on all of television.

Night of the Living Dead started a franchise that's been running on-and-off for half a decade. The end is in sight, though - Twilight of the Dead, “the seventh and final chapter of the Dead series, ” is in the works.

One of the next big paradigm-shifting moments in zombie horror came with Danny Boyle's 28 Days Later . The zombies here still follow the basic principles of insatiable undead fiends -- they want to kill you, a bite from them will infect and assimilate you, etc -- but these mf'ers would run at you, full speed, like insane hyenas. 1985's The Return of the Living Dead may have pre-dated this movie with fast ghouls, but 28 Days Later made it a craze.

Yes, fast-moving zombies became the new wave in terror. No longer were you surrounded by slow, moseying ghouls. No more sleepwalking hordes. This was like being pursued by a gang of maniacs.

Our growing anxieties over infectious diseases informed this malicious movie, about a secret laboratory "rage" virus exposed to the public. Starring Cillian Murphy, Naomie Harris, Brendan Gleeson, and Christopher Eccleston, 28 Days Later is post-apocalyptic perfection, reigniting the flames of the then-dying zombie genre and creating all new reasons to be terrified. Especially the idea of a hospitalized character waking up after a month and discovering that the entire world fell into ruin in such a brief window of time (something that The Walking Dead would echo when Robert Kirkman started the comic in 2003).

Let's backtrack a tiny bit and get goofy with Peter Jackson's 1992 film Braindead -- retitled Dead Alive for its North American release - which is a gore-filled, slapsticky Evil Dead 2-inspired affair about a young man, Lionel, whose mother is bitten by a "rat monkey." She dies and comes back to life as a ravenous reanimated corpse with a rather indiscriminate palate -- she even eats dogs!

The movie culminates with a sensational battle between a lawnmower-wielding Lionel and a horde of ruthless zombies (including their reanimated body parts), as well as a memorable final showdown with his now-grotesquely transformed mother. Braindead is splatter comedy gold, equal parts hilarious and disgusting. Yes, Zombies could be freakin' funny and Simon Pegg would list this film as a huge influence for Shaun of the Dead.

Ping-ponging back to something utterly terrifying, Rec is not only a tremendous zombie movie but it's also one of the best found-footage horror films of all time. This Spanish classic stars Manuela Velasco as a reporter who responds to an emergency call at a quarantined apartment building. Inside, an undead infection has spread and Rec becomes an absolutely nightmarish siege/survival story that utilizes the format brilliantly. Skip the American remake, 2008's Quarantine, and check out the original for some ground zero terror. Arguments can be made that the monsters in this aren't "zombies'' in the purest sense (it's a mix of rabies and...something biblical?) but we're not that pedantic.

Just when we thought fast-moving zombies may have run their course (after The Walking Dead almost fully dominated the zombie game last decade), Train to Busan dropped and absolutely devastated us. Managing to capture the intensity that World War Z was only partially successful with, Train to Busan is a basic "World quickly crumbling due to zombies everywhere" format done with expert flare and care. It's gripping, emotional, and next-level ferocious. One of the many films of the past 20 years that shined a much-deserved spotlight on South Korean cinema, Train to Busan utilized intense action, full characters, and social commentary to tell the tale of a father trying to get his young daughter somewhere, anywhere safe, as civilization dissolves from under their feet.

Launching into its scary story with only the slightest of explanations, George Romero's Dawn of the Dead , made 10 years after his original zombie game-changer, is both a thrill ride and a mood piece. Returning to the zombie genre he himself launched, Romero got to go bigger here in terms of production, special effects, and themes.

Ken Foree exudes calming authority as Peter, the S.W.A.T. team leader who anchors a foursome of refugees who hole up in a shopping mall after humanity discovers "there's no more room in hell." While much has been made in subsequent years of the film's running anti-consumerist commentary, the film proves to be much more interesting as a character study than a treatise on the dangers of too much shopping; but a healthy dose of ground-breaking gore combined with some wicked humor and considerable invention on the part of Romero make Dawn of the Dead a genre classic.

While the movie doesn't actually have any connection to the original Zombi (a recut-for-Europe version of Romero's Dawn of the Dead), this film sparked a zombie movie craze across Europe and made Italian filmmaker Lucio Fulci a horror icon. The flick follows a group of people searching for a missing man on a tropical island where a doctor is desperately searching for the cause of a recent epidemic of the undead. Zombi 2 is known for its sensational zombie antics -- such as the notorious eye-gouging, and jugular-biting moments -- as well as (wait for it...) zombie vs. shark wrestling! The 1979 movie was released in the U.S. as Zombie.

Ruben Fleischer's zany meta-take on zombie movies (that occasionally crosses over into parody) is a uproarious star-studded splatterfest with both action and heart. Zombieland stars Woody Harrelson, Jesse Eisenberg, Emma Stone, and Abigail Breslin as survivors of a zombie apocalypse who, after some comedic struggles, form a found-family in the midst of hell on Earth. All while trying to adhere to the "rules" of zombie apocalypse survival in order to best secure their future. At its core, Zombieland is a clever family road trip movie littered with undead dangers.

Zombie comedy isn't necessarily a recent thing, however. 1992's Braindead notwithstanding, The Return of the Living Dead landed in 1985 and emphasized laughs over screams.

After the release of the original Night of the Living Dead, director George Romero and his then-partner and co-writer John Russo went their separate ways to make their own follow-ups to the hugely successful film. Russo reportedly got the rights to the term "Living Dead," and that's how the Return series was born -- a group of films of greatly diminishing returns , so to speak, that bears some similarities to Romero's oeuvre but plenty of differences as well.

The original Return of the Living Dead remains a classic, standing tall above the pack due to writer-director Dan O'Bannon's (who wrote Alien's screenplay) comedic take on the material, as well as the now de rigueur zombie hunger for "braaaiiinnnsss!!!!!" that was first established here. O'Bannon's undead also distinguish themselves with their ability to run, and run fast, rather than simply stagger along, as well as with their inability to be "killed" (beyond incineration or having an A-bomb dropped on them, that is). And the unwinnable scenario that the director places his characters in is dark, dark, dark, despite the humor of the film.

The insane horror remake movement of the Aughts gave us a few good films, actually. One of them being Zack Snyder's re-do of Dawn of the Dead , which is a thrilling, mesmerizing spin on the original, now with fast-moving zombies. Snyder himself wouldn't break out big until 2007's 300 but this movie is still a fantastic display of harrowing edge-of-your-seat horror.

Dawn of the Dead once again features a ragtag group of survivors -- Ving Rhames, Sarah Polley, Jake Weber, and more -- in a "Mall of the Living Dead" siege scenario inside a Wisconsin shopping center. And while a few arguments can be made that it doesn't beat the original, in many ways it's a technically superior film with the advantage of modern-day make-up and visual effects.

Following in the social satire tradition of George Romero's zombie flicks, but played as a comedy rather than a straight-up horror film, Shaun of the Dead ranks as one of the most all-around entertaining zombie movies ever made. Telling the story of unambitious electronics salesman Shaun (Simon Pegg) as he races across town to save his girlfriend Liz (Kate Ashfield), who recently dumped him, from the undead, Shaun of the Dead boasts some great characters (including Shaun's best friend, Ed, played by Nick Frost), hilarious scenes, and very funny lines, all mixed in with some real scares that elevate it above stock zombie films. Shaun would stand proud as a calling card film for its two leads and director Edgar Wright as well as becoming the first installment in the Cornetto Trilogy (followed by Hot Fuzz and The World's End).

Check out more of the best comedy movies of all time .

The most recent film on our zombie list is probably also the least known zombie offering, truthfully. This Canadian horror outing imagines zombie uprising on an indigenous people's reserve, where the twist is that they're all immune to the undead plague because of their heritage. Blood Quantum has blood, carnage and a devilish socio-political twist that allows us to experience the genre through a different lens. It's a fascinating new take in a genre that's been done (pun intended) to death.

Let's follow up a lesser-known zombie flick with another under-the-radar project, since we're on a roll. The Girl with All the Gifts , based on the novel by M. R. Carey (who adapts his own book into a screenplay here), focuses on a team of scientists and soldiers escorting a young girl, Sennia Nanua's Melanie, in a world where a parasitic fungus has turned humans into mindless, murderous hordes. There are Last of Us vibes here as those involved hope to develop a cure based on children born in a half-state. Infected, yes, but with functioning minds and the ability to suppress their hunger. Glenn Close, Gemma Arterton, and Paddy Considine star in this scary, thought-provoking look at hope and survival.

Not only is Warm Bodies the only zombie rom-com (or one of a minuscule amount), but it's also rare in that it gives us the story from the zombie's point of view. Persistent charming and funny, Warm Bodies sends us into the infected mind of roaming ghoul "R" (Nicholas Hoult) as he falls dead over heels for a young woman named Julie (Teresa Palmer) as their eventual romance causes R to slowly return to human form, proving love can reawaken someone's life. It has humor, heart, and presents, overall, a clever twist on Romeo & Juliet.

Certainly left off of most hardline zombie lists, due to it being about science gone mad in a Dr. Frankenstein sort of way, but Stuart Gordon Re-Animator is a camp classic from the corner of shock and awe. Loosely based on a short story by H.P. Lovecraft, the film follows disgraced, driven medical student Herbert West (Jeffrey Combs) and his fellow classmate as they test out a serum that can bring dead tissue back to life. A cross between horror, deadpan comedy, and exploitation, The Re-Animator is buckets of gore clashing with buckets of gore mixed with barrels of laughs.

That's our pick of the 15 best zombie movies of all time! Has your favorite film made our list? If not, let us know in the comments.

Matt Fowler is a freelance entertainment writer/critic, covering TV news, reviews, interviews and features on IGN for 13+ years.

articles.title: Plans and Pricing - Paramount+ Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Paramount+ offers two standalone subscription plans with monthly and annual pricing plans. You can also choose to bundle the streaming service with Walmart+
articles.body:
Paramount+ offers two standalone subscription plans with monthly and annual pricing plans. You can also choose to bundle the streaming service with Walmart+ for additional savings.

Paramount+ has gone through several price reductions and increases since it first launched in 2021. After a price increase in January 2026 , this is the up-to-date pricing for both subscription tiers.

Both Essential and Premium subscribers get streaming on up to three devices, while only the Premium subscription offers downloads on those devices. The main difference between the two plans (other than ads) is whether or not you get access to Showtime, live TV, and 4K UHD streaming .

Should you decide you no longer want to subscribe, it's easy to cancel Paramount+ . Even after you cancel, access to the streaming service should still be available until the end of the billing period.

If you're looking for a deal on the standalone Paramount+ plans , there is one option currently available. Students over the age of 18 can get 50% off monthly or annual subscriptions for the first 12 months. After the first 12 months, the subscription goes back to full price.

Currently the best streaming bundle that includes Paramount+ is a Walmart+ subscription. One of the biggest benefits of a Walmart+ subscription are that you can access to Paramount+ streaming. You can also choose to switch between that and a Peacock Premium subscription every four months. Walmart offers both monthly and annual plans as well as a 30-day free trial for new subscribers.

As of January 15, 2026, Paramount+ is no longer directly offering a free trial. To get a free trial of the streaming service , you can try out a Walmart+ subscription for 30 days. There used to be a 7-day free trial included with the Prime Video add-on , but that offer has been removed as well.

articles.body:
Paramount+ first launched back in 2021 after being rebranded from CBS All Access. In addition to its broader content library from CNS, Nickelodeon, Comedy Central, and MTV, the streaming service has put out quite a few original shows in the last five years.

Most notably, Paramount+ is the home of everything in the Star Trek universe , including the newest shows. If you're looking for a full list of original shows you can watch with a Paramount+ subscription , we've got you covered right here. Some are even available to stream in 4K with a Premium plan.

With the merger of Paramount and Warner Brothers , it's still up in the air what will become of the original programming on Paramount+ and Warner Brothers' streamer, HBO Max . There are plans to eventually merge the two streaming platforms.

Note : We're only featuring original shows that premiered after the launch of Paramount+. Premiere dates are based on when the first episode became available in the U.S. and this list includes new releases for November 2026 an beyond.

articles.title: Plans and Pricing - Netflix Guide - IGN
articles.summary: As of the most recent March 2026 price increase, Netflix offers three different subscription plans. The least expensive plan includes ads and starts at $8.99,
articles.body:
As of the most recent March 2026 price increase , Netflix offers three different subscription plans. The least expensive plan includes ads and starts at $8.99, going up to the most expensive Premium plan at $26.99. The service has never participated in any type of streaming bundle, but is occasionally offered through select phone and internet plans.

Netflix previously offered a Basic plan that was discontinued in 2023.

Netflix does not offer a free trial for new subscribers . Even though the service does have a free trial page in the Netflix help center, it simply states that Netflix does not offer free trials and points to links on how to change your Netflix plan or cancel your membership .

Netflix was the service that pioneered TV streaming, which means it has the largest backlog of original shows and movies available online. If you want to watch popular shows like Stranger Things , Bojack Horseman , or the One Piece Live action series , the only place you can do so is on Netflix. articles.title: A Call from Beyond the Horizon - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: A Call from Beyond the Horizon is a Faction Quest that is part of the Charting the Unknown DLC category in Crimson Desert. This side quest sets you on a path
articles.body:
A Call from Beyond the Horizon is a Faction Quest that is part of the Charting the Unknown DLC category in Crimson Desert . This side quest sets you on a path to building your first ship for sailing the Pywel ocean. Learn how to get the Small Greymane Ship and what you'll need for it in this walkthrough!

A Call from Beyond the Horizon Walkthrough

Make your way over to Pailune , where you'll find three Greymanes chatting along the docks near the south side of town. They're not too far from a Street Vendor nearby as well. Once you've found them, talk to them to eavesdrop for a little before Kliff joins the conversation.

You'll learn that they're looking for a new way to make money and eventually settle on getting a boat. After hearing about an uncharted island that may be valuable, Kliff agrees with them on building a boat. Now you'll need to make your way over to Vellua to find the port there. If you're unsure of where to find it, you can find the fishing village far south below Hernand, where it's on the coast.

Upon arriving there, inspect Vellua to find the dispatch mission, Small Shipbuilding . You'll need the following supplies and comrades to complete it:

5 Greymanes, with at least one having the Engineering skill

After 12 in-game hours, the Small Shipbuilding dispatch mission will be complete. You can either focus on other activities during that time or try sleeping in a bed if you're not on a cooldown. Once the mission is done, the quest, A Call from Beyond the Horizon, is complete. This leads to the next quest, Where the Wind Blows .

articles.title: Where the Wind Blows - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Where the Wind Blows is a Faction Quest that is part of the Charting the Unknown DLC category in Crimson Desert. This side quest walks you through getting your
articles.body:
Where the Wind Blows is a Faction Quest that is part of the Charting the Unknown DLC category in Crimson Desert . This side quest walks you through getting your first ship ready for the open seas. Follow our walkthrough for help assigning staff to your ship and to avoid an easy mistake the game doesn't warn you about!

After finishing the previous quest, A Call from Beyond the Horizon , you'll now have your own boat. Before you can set sail, you'll need to travel to a few spots around the Vellua port. First, visit the Harbor Notice Board where two Greymanes are chatting. Speak to them to start a cutscene that finishes this objective. They'll chat about the bounty notices on the Notice Board that you can grab.

Once you're finished with these two, head toward the docks to find a Greymane holding a feather and pad . Speak to them to learn more about the valuable uncharted island that may have Azurite there. Before the cutscene here ends, a Greymane will hand you a Harpoon Gun. You'll eventually need this for underwater combat.

Now that you've finished these two quest objectives, you can go speak with the Ship Manager nearby. While you can buy a new ship here for a lot of Camp Funds, we don't recommend doing it quite yet. Especially since your Small Greymane Ship will work fine.

Make Sure to Get the Right Amount of Crew Before Sailing

While talking to the Ship Manager, press the Manage Crew button. Before departing, the quest will tell you to get three specific crew roles. However, you will need more than those for this quest. Here's who you'll need:

Fortunately, your comrades won't need any specific skills to man each role. Therefore, you can throw anyone into those slots. But you may want to prioritize stronger fighters in case enemies board your ship. And if you have enough Greymanes to fill the other crew roles, there's no reason not to.

Once you've assigned at least the crew roles we've mentioned, you can leave the Ship Manager. Then, head east down the pier to your boat . Hop onto it or climb the ladder to get on board. You can then operate the Ship's Wheel to complete Where the Wind Blows. This will activate a couple of windows that explain how sailing and ship combat work.

Continue over to the next quest in our walkthrough for the Charting the Unknown DLC, A Beginning Beyond the Waves . We'll give you some tips in that guide for how to sail with the wind as well as where to go.

articles.title: Families Who Lost Loved Ones in Seoul Halloween Crowd Crush Call on Activision to Pull Real Footage From Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
articles.summary: Bereaved families have called on Activision to remove real footage of the 2022 Seoul Halloween crush disaster from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
articles.body:
Bereaved families have called on Activision to remove real footage of the 2022 Seoul Halloween crush disaster from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 .

Modern Warfare 4, developed by Infinity Ward, thrusts players into the forefront of a North Korean invasion of South Korea. A video of real life rescue efforts from the crush in Itaewon, which led to the death of almost 160 people, appears briefly in Modern Warfare 4’s opening montage. We see footage but with a heavy filter and effects layered on top as part of the montage.

According to the BBC , the families issued a statement saying they were “appalled” that the footage was used in the game, and demanded Activision pull it.

"We cannot help but be appalled that the chaotic and desperate scene, in which many citizens at the site performed CPR to save one another and victims lay on the freezing street, was used as it was to create a scene in a game," the families said.

"Using such an event as material for a game made for entertainment is in itself highly inappropriate and senseless. If the game developer has even a minimum of courtesy and empathy towards the victims, it should take corrective action without delay."

In a statement issued to IGN, Activision said it used the footage to “establish the game’s fictional narrative.” It did not comment on the request to remove it from the game.

“In developing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, we approached the subject matter with care and respect. The game’s opening cinematic utilizes some real world news coverage to establish the game’s fictional narrative. It is not intended to reference or trivialize the Itaewon disaster or any other real-world tragedy in any way, shape or form.”

The crush occurred as mostly young people flooded the narrow, sloping streets of Itaewon to celebrate Halloween four years ago. An estimated 100,000 people packed the streets for the first virtually unrestricted Halloween festivities in three years following lockdowns. Witnesses said police had trouble controlling the crowds.

Responding to criticism from some quarters about setting the game in a fictional conflict that Koreans have real world concern about, Call of Duty's chief marketing officer, Tyler Bahl, told the BBC: "We have to understand this is entertainment.”

articles.body:
For November, Netflix has decided to onboard around 30 Christmas movies - most of them Hallmark shlock/slop from the past five years. No shade if that's your bag, but these bastards take up a huge slice of November's pumpkin pie. There's Christmas in castles, on ranches, on ships... basically anywhere and everywhere you'd like to holiday rom-com it up a full month early.

There's also a new Ron Howard-directed documentary about photographer Richard Avedon, the first three Insidious movies, the first two Resident Evils , Air Force One, Stand By Me, Smile, Looper, Bridesmaids, and a film called The Mummy (which could be four or five different movies from cinema history, just FYI).

And while this is far from its actual streaming debut, 2026 mega-hit Obsession also lands mid-November. You know, if you're looking for a good family watch during Thanksgiving.

If you're just looking for a detailed list of everything coming to Netflix in November, you can jump to the full release schedule by day.

Before The Last Jedi and the three Knives Out mysteries, writer/director Rian Johnson gave us the sci-fi dystopian mindbender Looper, featuring Bruce Willis and Joseph Gordon-Levitt as different aged versions of the same time-traversing cold-blooded contract killer. Emily Blunt, Paul Dano, and Jeff Daniels also star. High concept and a lot of fun.

This undermentioned gem from TV's Golden Era, created by Ray McKinnon, was Sundance TV's first original scripted series, starring Aden Young as Daniel, a man freed from prison after spending nearly 20 years on death row. Found not guilty due to new evidence, a traumatized Daniel must now reintegrate into society. This powerful, poignant drama also stars Abigail Spencer, J. Smith-Cameron, Adelaide Clemens, Clayne Crawford, and Luke Kirby

Bass X Machina , a new adult animated series from LeSean Thomas (Yasuke, Cannon Busters), is a steampunk take on legendary lawman Bass Reeves (voiced by Brian Tyree Henry). In THIS Wild West, brutal outlaws, machines, and supernatural terrors ravage the landscape, forcing Reeves to become judge, jury, and executioner. Janelle Monáe, Cree Summer, and Tati Gabrielle also lend their voices.

Carolina Caroline (movie, 2026) - November 6

Samara Weaving and Kyle Gallner star in this excellent-but-underseen crime thriller romance from this past summer. Directed by Adam Carter Rehmeier (who also directed Gallner in the great Dinner in America), Carolina Caroline follows a small-town Texas woman (Weaving) who embarks on a dangerous crime spree with a charismatic con man.

Shana Feste wrote and directed this new murder mystery, which stars Oscar-winner Jessica Chastain as a former country music star who comes out of seclusion and returns to Nashville after her rising-star singer-songwriter niece goes missing. John Hawkes, Garrett Hedlund, Carter Faith, and Jennifer Nettles also star.

I don't think anyone needs to be sold on this truly awesome, terrifying micro-budgeted movie. It's already reshaped the modern horror landscape as everyone now scrambles to find the next thing that costs very little that will make a whole lot. It's a simple enough Monkey's Paw-type tale, told expertly and filled with savage, scary layers. A groundbreaking performance by Inde Navarrette punctuates a gruesome campfire tale about agency, consent, and mistaking co-dependency and lust for love.

The Altruists (miniseries) - November 19

From writer Graham Moore (The Imitation Game), The Altruists is an eight-episode biographical miniseries about the collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX, and its sister trading firm, Alameda Research. Focusing on the tumultuous romance/partnership between FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried (Anthony Boyle) and Alameda co-CEO Caroline Ellison (Julia Garner), the series will bring to light the crimes and fraud of Gen Z's "Bonnie & Clyde."

articles.title: Get Ready for More Tales of the TMNT in 'Tear in Time' Sequel
articles.summary: If you're hungry for more Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, then check out our exclusive preview of the spinoff comic Tear in Time.
articles.body:
With Paramount having canceled the Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles animated series, and with the Mutant Mayhem sequel still a ways off, IDW Publishing remains the best and only source for new adventures set in this TMNT universe. Even as the publisher prepares to wrap up their second Tales of the TMNT comic , they're prepping another follow-up dubbed Tales of the TMNT: Tear in Time.

IGN can exclusively reveal a new preview of Tales of the TMNT: Tear in Time. Check out the slideshow gallery below to see cover art for issue #3 and early, uncolored interior artwork from issue #1:

Tales of the TMNT: Tear in Time Preview Gallery

The cover above is particularly noteworthy because it features the Turtles wearing costumes inspired by various other futuristic TMNT stories from years past. Michelangelo is wearing his TMNT: The Last Ronin costume, Donatello is wearing his Fast Forward costume, Raphael is wearing a costume from the 2003 animated series, and Leonardo is wearing his costume from Rise of the TMNT.

Tales of the TMNT: Tear in Time is written by Andrew Joustra and drawn by Louie Joyce. Both creators also provided IGN with some exclusive commentary about the new series:

I’m so excited to be going on more adventures with the turtles in Tales of the TMNT. Tear in Time will be my third arc for the series, and I’m thrilled that we have an opportunity to tell more stories and build out this corner of TMNT further. We’re not done yet and there's even more to come after Tear, but that'll remain a secret for now!

Not to be dramatic, but the fate of the entire Tales universe is at stake! This arc is massive in scale, bringing in characters from Mutant Mayhem, the Tales TV series and our previous arcs in the comics. I think it will help to establish Tales more firmly in the greater TMNT continuity with the inclusion of one of my other favorite characters from the franchise: Renet Tilley. I really wanted to give Renet an opportunity to shine and show some genuine growth in her character. She’s going to have her hands full, to say the least.

The finale of Coastal Chaos is also fast approaching, and the turtles will have to get creative in their next encounter with Armaggon. It’s clear that he has them outmatched in the water, so they concoct a plan to level the playing field. Armaggon won’t make it easy for them, so they’ll need to get some help from their Mutanimal friends if they want to save the city. And there’s a surprise you won’t want to miss in the final pages that help set up the events of Tear in Time…

One of the great things about drawing TMNT (y'know, beyond getting to draw mutated ninja turtles that are also teenagers) is how rich the supporting characters and wider universe is. There is so much to pull from! We've had a blast pulling in characters from the cartoon and movies and establishing new versions of characters like Fugitoid, Zog and Armaggon. With this new arc Andrew has crafted an epic story that takes the Tales universe and really widens the scope in a way we haven't seen yet!

Honestly, there's so much to tease with Tear in Time, but I don't think any words I type would do as good a job as the cover for issue 3 does! I had so much fun drawing this cover and it's always an honour to get to put your own little spin on something as iconic as the original TMNT #1 cover!

As for the final issue of Coastal Chaos, there's a big time mutant animal showdown at the docks! What more do ya need?

Tales of the TMNT: Coastal Chaos #3 will be released on November 18, followed by Tales of the TMNT: Tear in Time #1 on December 16. You can preorder both issues at your local comic shop .

In IGN's Tales of the TMNT review , Tyler Robertson wrote, "The first half of Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles never reaches the heights of Mutant Mayhem. But it still plants a unique flag in the ground by beautifully reimagining the film’s animation style, retaining most of the key elements that made Mutant Mayhem amazing, and telling a story that delves into the psyches of the individual Turtles. The return of Nicolas Cantu, Brady Noon, Shamon Brown Jr., and Micah Abbey and the personal journeys their characters embark on give us even more reason to care about the already-lovable versions of these iconic characters."

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Mass Effect 5 and BioWare Reportedly Died So Star Wars Battlefront 3 Could Live
articles.summary: BioWare reportedly shut down because EA bosses chose to invest in the development of Star Wars: Battlefront 3 over Mass Effect 5.
articles.body:
BioWare reportedly shut down because EA bosses chose to invest in the development of Star Wars: Battlefront 3 over Mass Effect 5.

Bloomberg reported that the main reason EA closed BioWare was because it had decided it could only afford to back one costly sci-fi action game, and Star Wars: Battlefront 3 was considered less of a risk than Mass Effect 5.

EA is under new financial pressures as a result of the $18 billion in debt it was saddled with in the wake of Saudi Arabia’s $55 billion leveraged buyout of the company. Bloomberg said that both Star Wars and Mass Effect were expected to cost hundreds of millions of dollars to produce, and despite the fact Battlefront 3 hadn’t even begun development, it was seen as a safer bet.

It didn’t help that BioWare’s recent games, Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard, had all failed commercially. Bloomberg also pointed to some internal politics that hurt BioWare’s cause within management.

BioWare had spent the past half decade teasing the next Mass Effect's setting and story before it was shut down last week. The shock news sparked an outpouring of affection for the studio's games, its staff past and present, and its legacy from fans and the video game community.

A trailer for Mass Effect 5 meant for internal purposes at BioWare soon leaked online , offering a glimpse at what might have been. The trailer, which IGN verified as legitimate, was created for EA leadership last year and was not meant for the public. The trailer has a number of familiar elements, including weaponry, powers, and alien species we've seen in previous Mass Effect games. There's a glimpse at a sex scene, a Mass Effect relay, space travel, and a nightclub, all of which are Mass Effect staples. There's even a galaxy map on display inside your ship.

According to Bloomberg , BioWare had around 50 staff working on Mass Effect 5 after EA gutted the studio following the failure of The Veilguard. This latest round of layoffs will see 400 jobs reportedly axed across EA, amounting to 3% of total staff. BioWare’s Austin studio reportedly remains open, working to support various EA games in development.

A petition to save Mass Effect is nearing 300,000 signatures, although there is no evidence to suggest EA would be willing to part ways with the franchise, even as it remains dormant. BioWare co-founder Greg Zeschuk, who alongside co-founder Ray Muzyka departed BioWare back in 2012, several months after the launch of Mass Effect 3, said the Saudi Public Investment Fund's $55 private buyout of EA was "the final nail in the coffin."

“I think that was the crux of it in a sense," he continued. "Once again it's a completely different company now... BioWare makes these kind of unusual games that take a long time and they're complicated and so it's easier just to pump out sports games every year and that's a better business model in some ways.”

11 Mass Effect Characters and Moments the TV Show Needs to Be a Hit

Amazon's Mass Effect TV show for Prime Video remains in the works , despite the end of BioWare and the cancellation of Mass Effect 5. Star Wars: Battlefront 3, meanwhile, is in the works at Respawn and DICE, although we know next to nothing about it.

articles.title: RTX 5080 Disappears From Nvidia's Store as Prices Reach $2,000
articles.summary: As the RAM crisis has played out in 2026, graphics cards have been hit particularly hard, due to the high-performance memory that's stapled onto the things. And now it seems like the RTX 5080 may have been discontinued.
articles.body:
As the RAM crisis has played out in 2026 , graphics cards have been hit particularly hard, due to the high-performance memory that's stapled onto the things. And now it seems like the RTX 5080 may have been discontinued.

After the RTX 5090 appeared to have been discontinued , the RTX 5080 has also disappeared from Nvidia's GeForce Marketplace , but there might be a replacement on the way. It's possible Nvidia is getting ready to replace the 16GB RTX 5080 with a 24GB model, though.

Most recently, a post on ChannelGate (via Club386 ), which tracks the tech supply chain in China, suggested that Nvidia is going to discontinue the original 5080, and replace it with a 24GB version as early as december. But while that would help the supply issue, with the price of memory right now, a 24GB graphics card is going to be even pricier.

This isn't the first time we've seen rumors of mid-generation graphics cards from Nvidia, though. Rumors for the RTX 50 Super series started spinning up late last year, only to supposedly be discontinued due to the RAM shortage all the way back in February .

For now, the most powerful consumer GPU you can buy from Nvidia's marketplace is the RTX 5070 Ti , which is a step down from the 5080. But, because prices are what they are right now, the 5070 Ti, which launched for $749 in 2025, will set you back at least $1,299 at the time of writing – which is more than the RTX 5080 launched for.

Even the RTX 5070 will set you back at least $849 on Nvidia's storefront right now, which is a huge increase over its $549 launch price.

If you do want to get your hands on the RTX 5080 right now, it is still possible, but I'm not sure how well stock is going to hold out. The cheapest 5080 I can find on Newegg is a Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4 edition from MSI, which will set you back $1,899 – nearly twice the 5080's $999 launch price. Over on Micro Center, every RTX 5080 is listed as "store pickup only," with the cheapest model being a Gigabyte Windforce card for $1,979. And, that particular card is out of stock in every location in New York, at least.

Even though you can still buy a 5080 if you have an astronomical budget, it sure seems like the high-end graphics card is on the cusp of being discontinued, or at least becoming so scarce that it might as well be. I've reached out to Nvidia for comment, and I'll update this story if and when I hear back, but we might be entering a period where the two most powerful gaming cards are essentially unobtainable.

It is possible that the 24GB RTX 5080 is real, and maybe we really will see it in December or even at CES 2027. But Samsung, which manufactures most of Nvidia's graphics memory, just claimed in its latest earnings call that the RAM shortage is only going to get worse in 2027 , so I can only imagine how expensive this newfangled 24GB 5080 is going to be.

articles.title: Here's What Really Happened at the End of Yaga Episode 3 in That Shocking Twist
articles.summary: Yaga’s third episode envelopes us further with its otherworldly occurrences and shocking reveals, while keeping us on our toes for who’s really behind the mysteries and possible horrors that seem to lie ahead.
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Yaga Season 1, Episode 3. Episodes 1-3 are now streaming on AMC+ in the US and Crave in Canada, with new episodes releasing on Fridays at midnight PT.

Yaga Episode 3 wastes no time diving right back into this eerie, witchy tale, while answering some of our biggest questions after last week’s debut.

We pick up right where Episode 2’s cliffhanger left off – on the beach with Logan’s body – prior to getting confirmation from the police that, yes, it is in fact Logan’s lifeless body (not Henry’s) and that blood was found near a window open in his bedroom. There’s a moment of confusion for the viewer as Rapp sees Logan’s eyes jump open, and we see that they are ice blue – like Henry’s.

By now, we know Rapp has been hallucinating more frequently and this is possibly either from the drugs from the night before (because he honestly looks like he’s still high) or something dark and ominous that’s happening to him.

We see a pattern in relation to “time” in Yaga. This is confirmed when Carson recounts what happened the previous night at Henry’s party where we learn that “a few hours” had passed between seeing Logan disappear into his room upstairs, and Carson finding Rapp on the beach. Originally, it seemed like some time had passed, but nothing substantial.

As we continue on with more unexplained moments in this story, Rapp tries to put a move on Carson in his hotel room, which she rejects. He then goes to lie down on his bed and falls asleep almost too quickly – Carson comes and kneels down next to the bed and we see the clock turn to 3:33 (not the first time we’ve seen this either), while intense, whispering voices begin to take over as she leans in to almost kiss him. Rapp gently opens his eyes and sees Pam, Henry’s ex-girlfriend, seductively pulling a white feather out of his mouth.

He suddenly jolts out of his actual sleep and awakens some time later in the day. We also notice a small circle tattoo on Carson’s wrist before they head over to forensics, which seems to be placed in the shot intentionally for us to refer back to later…

Going to the mortuary, we see Logan’s corpse – well, most of it. In the episode’s biggest WTF moment, we learn Logan’s penis was severed from his body and he was castrated. It turns out he was also stabbed with an ancient knife made out of Obsidian and human bone – which Katherine later classifies as an Aztec ceremonial midwife sacrificial knife, connected to deities with symbols representing sexual desire and fertility. All signs so far point to Logan being murdered, and Carson and the police on staff are searching for more evidence, especially as this new case potentially relates to Henry.

We see Carson walk up to a small church to meet Logan’s mom, Alice (played by Sarah Strange). The dark, moody shots and heavy music come together to create an emotionally beautiful scene of grief between the two women. They sit on a bench in the cemetery together and more is revealed about Logan that we hadn’t known before. That includes Logan changing his hair and working out constantly – like he was trying to become Henry himself, perhaps.

Alice reveals her hate for the Parks and shares how she heard a rumor that Logan and Henry bought one of Pam’s lame hens from her and joked they were going to sacrifice it. She then explains passionately how she could see everything affecting Logan, saying, “Everyday, I’d see that thing growing in him. That thing getting bigger and thicker and darker and pulling him further and further away from God, and closer and closer to the Devil.” Carson asks about Logan’s dad, but Alice dismisses the questions.

While Carson is with Alice, we see Rapp jogging on the beach. Pam happens to be running in front of him. He tries to catch up to her and, as he does, she all of a sudden splits into three versions of herself, distorted in Rapp’s view. She calls his name and he trips over a log, seeing more visions and a sinister mask staring back at him, as he peers up at Pam who is somehow immediately next to him with a cheeky comment.

Before Carson and Rapp decide to head back over to Henry’s house to check for more leads, Carson inquires if Henry and Logan were possibly in a relationship, giving Rapp unintentional fuel to speculate on Carson’s sexuality as well, which she avoids divulging.

As the duo begin surveying Logan’s room, you can see the pile of bloodied sheets next to the window, and they begin slowly uncovering more and more clues as they go along. Interestingly, they find drug powder in a canister with the same triangle symbol we saw from the previous episodes – a symbol known as the Triskelion – which has multiple interpretations. In Celtic mythology it is said to represent sacred femininity and the Triple Goddess archetype: the Maiden, the Mother, and the Crone. Baba Yaga in Slavic folklore is known as the “Crone,” so we’ll have to wait and see how that relates (if at all) as the series continues.

Carson and Rapp also notice the chicken foot hanging from Logan’s lampshade, previously in Henry’s room – and we can now pretty safely assume it’s from the chicken he and Henry were rumored to have sacrificed.

Just when they are trying to figure out how Logan disappeared from his room the night before, Rapp discovers the bookshelf is actually a secret door into another room… a small, eerie spot illuminated by red lights, despite the rest of the house having no power. A desk with a tape recorder and an archive of dozens upon dozens of cassette tapes are stacked on shelves.

As they dig in further, Carson and Rapp find out there’s a recording from the previous night in Henry’s bedroom – from when Logan was having sex with the woman wearing the angel wings. We hear Logan demanding to be called “Henry,” making us wonder if Henry was even at the party last night – despite his phone being traced to that location.

Rapp searches through Henry’s room, discovering – disturbingly – a wired bug hidden on his nightstand, which is triggered to record in Logan’s “secret office” whenever someone speaks in the room. Carson plays more of the recording from the prior night and they discover Pam is the one who was having sex with Logan, just hours before his death – making her officially a suspect in Logan’s murder.

As we’re processing that surge of information, Rapp’s eyes suddenly catch on a drop of blood on the floor next to the bed – he drops down and peers under, seeing something bloody smeared on the floor. He quickly pulls the bed back, pushing it out of the way, and as Carson comes into the room we see the Triskelion symbol drawn wide across the floor in blood, with three white chicken feathers near each point in the symbol – seemingly signifying a curse or some kind of spell. It’s even more eerie with the haunting music, which pulls you into its claws and feels like a spell wrapping itself tightly around you, right as Baba Yaga narrates through the end of the episode.

We see solid character development in this episode, with Clark Backo stepping more into her role as Carson and raising the question of where her boundary lies between professionalism and intrigue. Noah Reid as Rapp brings more grit to his role and shows a darker, more intense side to his character – I’m looking forward to seeing how both of these characters expand into this world from here.

Some lingering questions we now have going into Episode 4: Do Henry and Logan have the same dad and is that why Alice despises the Parks so much? Is Pam a witch or maybe Baba Yaga in disguise? Did Logan put the spell under Henry’s bed, and if so, why and who’s really behind it?

articles.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman Thinks It's 'Terrible' for You to Have RAM in Your Gaming PC
articles.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman thinks it's "terrible" for people to have RAM in their computers rather than in a data center, as the scarcity of memory caused by the AI boom continues to drive up costs.
articles.body:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman thinks it's "terrible" for people to have RAM in their computers rather than in a data center, as the scarcity of memory caused by the AI boom continues to drive up costs.

In an interview with YouTuber Cheeky Pint , Altman talked about the global compute supply problems facing the AI industry right now. And, when the conversation inevitably moved on to memory, Altman claimed that the "invisible hand" (of the market) is failing, likely because every DRAM wafer isn't flowing straight into a data center to run these AI models.

Altman said: "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and being used maybe 5% of the time. Like, you want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that."

It kind of makes sense from Altman's perspective. It's in OpenAI's best interest to get as many hyperscaler data centers online to make its huge AI models as fast as possible. But, while Altman seems to believe that everyone is buying memory just to run local AI models, RAM is needed for nearly every kind of consumer electronics product, which is why every piece of gaming hardware has risen in price this year.

Just this month, used PS5 Pros skyrocketed in price to $1,399 , after the console got an official price increase in March due to the RAM shortage. Meanwhile, the RTX 5080 just disappeared off of Nvidia's marketplace, weeks after the RTX 5090 was all but discontinued .

For Altman, though, who believes cloud-based AI models are the future of computing, it's likely he sees all of these consumer shortages as a way to ensure that more memory gets funneled to AI companies to stuff it into data centers. And, according to Samsung's latest earnings call , that's exactly what's happening, and is why the RAM situation isn't going to get any better next year.

articles.title: With Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, a Majestic Epic Falls Victim to Eye-Sore CGI, Awkward AI Lip-Syncing, and More
articles.summary: Review: With Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, a majestic epic falls victim to clunky action, eye-sore CGI, and awkward AI lip-syncing in what is, unfortunately, just a Part 1.
articles.body:
Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is in theaters beginning Nov. 5.

Hindi cinema has long looked to Hollywood as a benchmark for big-screen action; much of its 21st century style, for instance, was inspired by Mission: Impossible 2 . Ramayana: Rise of a Legend re-imagines the resplendent Hindu epic as a CGI-laden blockbuster at a time when the Marvel Cinematic Universe has become the de facto touchstone for big-budget adaptations. In that vein, Nitesh Tiwari’s undertaking does, in fact, resemble a Marvel movie. Unfortunately, that Marvel movie happens to be Thor: Love and Thunder , a much-derided film whose floating head VFX had to be famously reworked .

This resemblance takes hold in an early scene, in which the epic’s antagonist, Ravana (charismatic Toxic star Yash), prays atop a cliff to the creator-god Brahma, whose countenance takes the form of a disembodied constellation with an overly-expressive digital mouth. This excess fluidity is owed, in part, to the movie’s uncanny English dub, which was shown to press in the United States in lieu of the original Hindi version (which happens to be 18 minutes longer than this 162-minute cut). Rather than traditional dubbing, the filmmakers developed their own in-house Generative A.I. technology (fittingly called Brahma A.I.) to sync up the characters’ lips to the flowery English dialogue. Some are calling it the future of cinema, but in its current incarnation, the result resembles exaggerated mouth movements superimposed on still images for comedy sketches, à la The Annoying Orange .

This effect is befitting of such a robotic adaptation, one which briefly threatens to interrogate the several millennia-old text of the title (in the vein of recent Thai drama The Burning Giants , which critiques the violence at the heart of national myths) before locking itself into a didactic approach. It’s a rigid depiction of both the subcontinent-spanning plot, as well as the theme of “Dharma,” or sacred duty, which the characters verbalize ad nauseum and follow unconditionally, and uninspiringly. For the uninitiated — which is to say, Sony’s target audience for the English dub, whose Indian subtitle (“Part 1”) has been slyly replaced with “Rise of a Legend” to convince people they’re paying for a complete story — the plot concerns an ongoing war between demigods the Devas and demons the Asuras.

The film re-imagines the villainous Ravana as a kind of liberator gone mad. The Asura leader begins by praying for the power to free his enslaved clan, and his island kingdom of Lanka, from Deva oppression before conquering nearby cities through violent conquest with his ambitious siblings by his side.. This forces the demigods to turn to the protector deity Vishnu, who re-incarnates himself as the human-born Rama (Ranbir Kapoor), one of four princes of the kingdom of Ayodhya. Prologues pile up on prologues for nearly an hour, as Rama grows up learning the ways of war and wisdom, since his divine destiny is to defeat the Asuras for good.

However, the filmmakers’ decision to cleave the story in half leaves it hanging in suspended animation. It ends where the central plot of the Ramayana — Rama’s journey to rescuing his devoted wife Sita (Sai Pallavi) from Ravana’s clutches — finally kicks off in earnest, yielding an episodic experience where the central hero and villain are, at best, vaguely aware of one another’s existence. They never actually come into contact, leaving Ramayana: Rise of a Legend with the responsibility of establishing a protagonist and antagonist alluring enough that viewers with no pre-existing religious or cultural attachment will feel dutybound to return in one year’s time — or whenever the sequel is ready.

How does this work out? As far as Ravana is concerned, Kannada-language superstar Yash makes a meal of the character, imagined as an action anti-hero who dances in fiery worship of the destroyer god Shiva, and who nails his enemies with jackknife powerbombs , as vengeful gears turn slowly in his mind. Traditionally depicted with 10 heads side by side, the movie’s version of Ravana re-imagines this as a kind of fissure of personality, wherein 10 different versions of the demon king (some old, some young; some confident, some sniveling) converse and argue within his consciousness. He’s ruthless in one moment, but respectful in the next, making for the closest thing the movie has to complexity before it returns to the story’s binary good-versus-evil traditions. Add to this the fact that the movie’s Lanka is vibrant, energetic and sensual, compared to its stilted, austere Ayodhya, and it becomes hard to root for the ostensible “good guys.”

Unfortunately, this becomes doubly true whenever Rama is on screen. The film’s depiction of him is an utter bore. An embodiment of virtue in the abstract, the heroic prince — who agrees to live in exile for 14 years so one of his brothers can take the throne — is spoken of as a kind and capable figure, but his people’s worship of him is a default setting, rather than something earned through benevolence. After all, Rama is a central figure in Hinduism, so more than enough viewers will bring their own baggage to the movie. But as a story, it’s as rote as can be, a flaw that infects its dramatic DNA: Rama’s relationship to Sita. While Pallavi is afforded a tad more action and autonomy than most actresses in the role, the promise of a sword-wielding Sita is often cut short, returning her quickly to a two-dimensional damsel who shares little chemistry with her husband. Much like Kapoor’s Rama, Pallavi’s Sita is graceful in posture, but there’s little underlying either of them as actual human beings.

Rama, who lacks anything resembling outward opinions or an inner life beyond his Dharma, acquires weapons and knowledge not through practice or learning, but through gurus psychically unlocking these hidden abilities, as though the film were operating on video game logic. Each new chapter sees him “leveling up” as he fights a different, malformed CGI golem in a new forest setting, though at least he deserves credit for using his unlimited magical arrows to get these eyesores off our screens.

Saddled with clunky English dialogue, Kapoor is the perfect actor for this version of Rama, but that’s not the compliment it seems. His po-faced approach snaps perfectly into place, alongside a dramatically dull incarnation of the mythic hero, whose duty toward violent reprisal, and whose adoration by his legions of fans, is a given. Kapoor, a fourth generation Bollywood star, enjoys exactly such a quasi-religious fandom, even if the Hindu nationalist factions the film has been courting with its marketing (which refers to these myths as “history”) has since turned on him for eating meat — a religious faux pas among Hindutva extremists.

Then again, with the movie’s attempts to stoke religious fervor being all but cancelled out, perhaps it makes sense to approach Ramayana: Rise of a Legend as a hermetically sealed experience, if only for a moment. This doesn’t do it any favors either; aesthetically, it’s a headache. While the grandeur of the costumes and archaic sets might draw one’s gaze in static moments, the cumulative effect of its many action scenes is often bewildering. Sure, some individual shots are big and bold in composition, but they’re frenetic and unfocused when strung together, with points of interest shifting in and out, left and right, and up and down at random. The fantasy fights lack the necessary physical and emotional weight to make a lasting impact, even before Rama’s fellow exiled brother Lakshmana (Ravi Dubey) delivers his umpteenth comic quip met by awkward dead air, adding to the Marvel-ness of it all.

Hans Zimmer and A.R. Rahman join hands for some booming compositions, but the music — much of which has been trimmed for the shorter cut, which features little singing or dancing — is tasked with scoring scenes and set pieces with no rhythm of their own. The film feels entirely off-kilter even before characters open their distracting, digitally-rendered mouths. That some of them sound like whiny, posh South Bombay youngsters is, perhaps, something only viewers who’ve spent time in India might really notice in the English version, but it nonetheless robs the dialogue-heavy drama of its potential grandeur.

There are fleeting pluses to be found throughout the runtime. The movie, for instance, features one moment of evocative suggestion — a harsh cut from a nightmarish vision to an empty throne, denoting the weight of Rama’s regal responsibility — but anything resembling moral dilemma is quickly swallowed by prescriptive plot developments, which leave little room for meaningful character arcs or emotional possibility. A climactic mid-air battle does, quite mercifully, manage to capture the imagination without much haphazard distraction. However, this scene doesn’t actually involve Rama at all. Its focus, instead, is a supporting character barely glimpsed up until that point, leaving Kapoor’s dreary protagonist to promise a more cogent narrative in the sequel.

The duology’s success is all but guaranteed in India and among its diaspora, given how deeply entrenched the Ramayana remains in Hindu and Indian culture (its release coincides with the major festival Diwali). However, to anyone not already attuned to the tale, it’s hard to imagine this version being a meaningful enough introduction to bring novice viewers back. It has neither the emotional hook nor the soul to compensate for its lack of visual momentum, and its reliance on a half-baked tech to appeal to a wider audience impedes what little drama exists at its core.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 Rating Potentially Leaks Port for Original 2009 FPS
articles.summary: The Australian Classification Board has rated Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, suggesting a port of Infinity Ward's original 2009 shooter may soon be revealed.
articles.body:
The Australian Classification Board has rated Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 , suggesting a port of Infinity Ward's original 2009 shooter may soon be revealed.

The ACB updated its website to reflect a fresh R 18+ rating for the fan-favorite entry in the Activision franchise, with a classification date of October 1, 2026, as spotted by Insider Gaming . Reflecting a mature description based on instances of "high-impact drug use, in-game purchases, online interactivity and chat," the sudden appearance of a rating suggests Microsoft may have plans to revisit Modern Warfare 2 in the near future.

The page, which is still live at the time of this piece's publication, specifically calls the title "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009)." As many others have already pointed out, the obvious assumption is that this is our first hint that a proper port will soon be revealed. Which platforms it may appear on was not shared, but fans may want to stay on their toes for an announcement.

There is one major reason to suspect Modern Warfare 2 (2009) may soon return: Activision tried the same strategy with the Black Ops series earlier this year. Ports for Black Ops 1 and 2 were leaked , announced , and launched all within the span of about one month back in June – and seemingly to much success. Black Ops 2, specifically, reportedly emerged as one of the best-selling games of the year in the month after its launch, but Activision's decision to replay its hits didn't arrive without controversy.

Many criticized the Call of Duty ports as "low effort," calling out both Black Ops games for being little more than direct rips of the original 2010s releases with few, if any, upgrades. There was also the issue of exploiters, as multiplayer lobbies quickly populated with players more interested in taking advantage of the level-up system than actually playing the game . Activision eventually looked into the issue .

While tech and gameplay problems soured an otherwise exciting moment for Call of Duty fans, both ports' prices didn't do the release any favors either. Each game cost $40 on PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5. DLC was also sold separately, with fans of the add-on content asked to spend $29.99 for each season pass if they didn't want to purchase any content individually. Discounts for PlayStation Plus subscribers helped soften the blow, but players will probably be on the lookout for similar issues should a Modern Warfare 2 port pop up.

Microsoft and Activision brought both Black Ops 1 and 2 ports exclusively to PlayStation consoles in July. Which platforms Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009) may launch for, or if ports for other early entries in the Modern Warfare series will show up, remains to be seen. We'll have to wait for Activision to confirm the news to learn more.

IGN gave Infinity Ward's 2009 Call of Duty game a 9.5/10 review upon its release. For more, you can read about the developer who said it was "hard to watch" Xbox profit from its recent Black Ops ports . You can also check out the ambience website that lets you fall asleep to the sound of old-school CoD lobbies .
